questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All A are M.

II. No M is B.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some M are A.

II. Some B are M.

III. Some A are B.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follows
Both conclusions II and III follows

questions.solution:
Statements:

I. All A are M.

II. No M is B.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a4845507676edaaba564fb397f120d30b28115e5051ddb08966ec3a2dbe5cb7.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some M are A → True (It is given that all A are M, so some M are A)

II. Some B are M → False (No direct relationship given between B and M, so it may be possible but not defined)

III. Some A are B → False (No direct relationship given between A and B, so it may be possible but not defined)\

Hence,** "Only conclusion I follows"**.

questions.question:
By interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be not correct?

+ and ×, 5 and 4

I. 4 + 8 × 5 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

II. 5 × 3 – 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = –8
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

I. 4 + 8 × 5 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

After interchanging the signs + and ×, and numbers, 5 and 4 in the given equation, we have

5 × 8 + 4 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

Applying BODMAS Rule, we get

5 × 8 + 4 – 7 = 37

⇒ 40 + 4 – 7 = 37

⇒ 44 - 7 = 37

⇒ 37 = 37

The given equation is correct.

II. 5 × 3 – 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = –8

After interchanging the signs + and ×, and numbers, 5 and 4 in the given equation, we have

4 + 3 – 5 × 6 ÷ 2 = –8

Applying BODMAS Rule, we get

4 + 3 – 5 × 3 = –8

⇒ 4 + 3 – 15 = –8

⇒ 7 – 15 = –8

⇒ -8 = –8

The given equation is correct.

Hence, **"****Neither I nor II****"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some clowns are artists.

All artists are smart.

All smarts are rich.

**Conclusions:**

I. All artists are rich.

II. Some clowns are smart.

III. All clowns are artists.

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Statements:

Some clowns are artists.

All artists are smart.

All smarts are rich.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13120b2d08591ddcd8feae4f330304f47c2d757d44224a0eb508fe681fedb3f4.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All artists are rich → Follow → Since 'All artists are smart..' & 'All smarts are rich.' we can say that All artists are rich and the same can be seen in the Venn diagram so the conclusion follows

II. Some clowns are smart → Follow → Since 'Some clowns are artists.' & 'All artists are smart.' we can say that Some clowns are smart and the same can be seen in the Venn diagram so the conclusion follows

III. All clowns are artists → Does not follow → From the given statements 'Some clowns are artists' which means Clown is subset of Artists, therefore All clowns are artists is a possibility not necessity so the conclusion does not follow.

Hence, **Both conclusions I and II follow.**

questions.question:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

60 × 3 + 660 ÷ 6 – 20 = 290
questions.solution:
**Given:**

60 × 3 + 660 ÷ 6 – 20 = 290

**Calculation:**

By option Method:

**Option 1: exchange **6 and 660, × and ÷

⇒ **60 ÷ 3** + **6 x 660** – 20 = 290

⇒ 20 + 3960 - 20 = 290 

⇒ 3960 ≠ 290

This is not correct the equation.

**Option 2: exchange **20 and 6, + and -

⇒ **60 × 3** - **660 ÷ 20** + 6 = 290

⇒ 180 - 33 + 6 = 290

⇒ 153 ≠ 290

This is not correct the equation.

**Option 3: exchange **20 and 60, + and × 

⇒ 20 + **3 x 660 ÷ 6** – 60 = 290

⇒ 20 + 330 -60 = 290

⇒ 290 = 290

This is correct the equation.

**Option 4: exchange **20 and 660, + and ÷

⇒ **60 × 3 ÷ 20** + 6 – 660 = 290

⇒ 9 + 6 - 660 = 290

⇒ -645 ≠ 290

This is not correct the equation.

Hence, **'Option 3'** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

81 + 3 ÷ 9 * 5 − 12 = 60
questions.solution:
**Given:**

81 + 3 ÷ 9 * 5 − 12 = 60

**Calculation:**

By option Method:

**Option 1: exchange **÷ and +

⇒ **81 ÷ 3** + **9 * 5** − 12 = 60

⇒ 27 + 45 -12 = 60

⇒ 60 = 60

This is correct the equation.

**Option 2: exchange **+ and *

⇒ **81 * 3 ÷ 9** + 5 − 12 = 60

⇒ 27 +5 - 12 = 60

⇒ 20 ≠ 60

This is not correct the equation.

**Option 3: exchange **÷ and –

⇒ 81 + 3 - **9 * 5 ÷ 12** = 60

⇒ 81 + 3 - 3.75 = 60

⇒ 80.25 ≠ 60

This is not correct the equation.

**Option 4: exchange **+ and –

⇒ 81 - **3 ÷ 9 * 5** + 12 = 60

⇒ 81 - 1.66 + 12 = 60

⇒ 91.34 ≠ 60

This is not correct the equation.

**∴ Interchanges (÷ and +) would make the given equation correct.**
